title: Design System: Quiet Ledger

surface-zebra.note: Subtle alternating-row tint for the holdings + watchlist register rows (~1.5% delta from surface in light, ~3.5% in dark). Dark mode pair: oklch(21.5% 0.008 60) — bumped 2026-05-14 from 20.5% so the alternation reads in dark too. Added 2026-05-13 with the register-row primitive.

accent.note: v4 SWS rewrite (2026-05-19): replaced the v3 muted rust accent. Dark #D9B97A, light #B89968. Exposed as --accent-primary; --accent is an alias. Hex, not OKLCH — the sanctioned v4 exception. Single shared accent: nav underline, focus rings, tick-pulse, snowflake fill/stroke, gold portfolio line.

accent-strong.note: Focus-visible ring escalation only. Light pair oklch(58% 0.10 80).

gain.note: Chart strokes only (sparkline, price chart). Muted forest; quiet tier. Always paired with up arrow + sign. Distinct from the loud accent-success used in chips. Dark pair oklch(62% 0.11 145).

loss.note: Chart strokes only. Muted sienna; quiet tier. Always paired with down arrow + sign. Distinct from the loud accent-danger used in chips. Dark pair oklch(62% 0.13 25).

slice-1.note: Sequential graphite ramp (slice-1..7) for donut + concentration/currency stacks. Largest = darkest in light; ramp INVERTS in dark (largest = lightest) so the largest position still reads heaviest on the near-black surface.

accent-success.note: v4. Positive KPI deltas, check statement-card icons, 'undervalued' framing. Light #009244. Loud tier — never a chart stroke.

accent-warn.note: v4. warn statement-card icons, 'overvalued' framing. Light #C25F1F. Loud tier.

accent-danger.note: v4. Negative KPI deltas, low-score dividend chips. Light #BC0024. Loud tier.

display.purpose: Plex Sans Light 300, text-5xl. Hero USD total only. One per page.

display-serif.purpose: IBM Plex Serif Medium 500. The only serif type in the system, display-only: portfolio masthead h1 (text-3xl) + dividend income hero (text-4xl, gold) + the ƒ ex-div glyph (serif italic). Added in the v4 SWS rewrite.

headline.purpose: Section anchors when prose introduces a block.

title.purpose: Card headings, ticker names, drill-in subheaders.

body.purpose: Default reading text. Insight prose, anomaly translations, position notes.

label.purpose: Recurring section caption. The single most-used type role.

numeric.purpose: Tabular figures via .tabular class on every numeric cell.

mono.purpose: Inline <code> + macro-event ticker labels in the calendar (font-mono uppercase). Numbers do not switch to mono.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: The only transition in the system. Applied to row hover, nav tab hover, theme toggle hover, sortable header hover, textarea focus.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all transitions and animations zeroed via prefers-reduced-motion: reduce

narrative.overview:
The dashboard is a paper-and-ink ledger for a long-horizon investor, a place for sitting with positions, not reacting to them. Warm graphite type rests on cream in light mode; in dark mode (the v4 default) paper-cream ink rests on an SWS-style cool near-black (hue ~240). One rare gold accent carries interactive emphasis. Numbers are reported with the same typographic gravity at 0.2% as at 5%; the data does the talking, not the chrome. Mercury for restraint, Linear for craft, Notion for the canvas-as-page feel.

Explicitly not a Bloomberg full-clone, not Robinhood, not the generic LLM SaaS dashboard. The reading room rejects all three by construction.

Three top-level routes (/, /portfolio, /watchlist) share a single max-w-6xl column and a NavBar (lowercase masthead + 3-tab ink-underline strip + a locale toggle EN/中 and a 2-state dark<->light theme toggle). / and /watchlist stay thin; /portfolio is itself split into six query-param tabs (?tab=holdings|returns|updates|dividends|analysis|calendar, parsed server-side) - the weekend-study surface where the SWS primitives (snowflake, KPI strip, statement cards, comparison gauges, dividend ledger) live. The whole surface is fully localized en/zh. Tokens are CSS custom properties in web/src/app/globals.css; since v4 dark is the default (defaultTheme="dark", enableSystem=false). Both modes are first-class.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-cream (light) / cool near-black (dark) surface, inverting ink, one rare SWS gold accent.
Plex Sans + Plex Mono for the working surface; Plex Serif (v4) reserved for display h1s + the dividend income hero. Tabular figures opt-in on numeric cells.
Flat by default; depth from spacing, hairline borders, and tonal contrast. v4 adds bordered rounded-xl SWS cards (bg-surface-raised) for the study-mode primitives - still shadowless.
Two densities (glance, study) sharing one visual vocabulary; drill-in / portfolio-tab, not switch-of-surface, is how density scales.
Color never carries meaning alone; gain/loss always paired with arrow + sign; statement sentiment always paired with a check/warn/neutral glyph.
Charts that ship in SSR HTML are hand-rolled SVG (sparkline, donut, stacks, benchmark line, snowflake radar, dividend bar); Recharts only inside the lazy-mounted drill-in price chart.
Restrained motion: state changes only; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce zeroes all transitions and animations globally.

rules.name: The Two-Tier Color Rule
rules.body: Color works in two registers. The quiet tier (muted forest gain / sienna loss + the graphite slice ramp) owns everything occupying chart real estate (sparklines, price chart, donut, stacked bars). The loud tier (SWS green success / red danger / orange warn) is confined to small bounded UI: chips, single KPI deltas, statement-card icons. Gold is the single shared interactive accent across both. A chart never uses the loud tier; a chip never uses gold for up/down.

rules.name: The OKLCH Doctrine (with v4 exception)
rules.body: Surfaces, ink, rule, gain/loss, and slices are OKLCH in a narrow chroma band so neutrals belong to one family. The v4 accent + status tokens (accent-primary, success, warn, danger) ship as hex matched from the SWS palette — the one sanctioned departure from the all-OKLCH doctrine.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The gold accent is used on <=10% of any screen. Its rarity is the message. Two accents on one view is one accent too many.

rules.name: The No-Sole-Signal Rule
rules.body: Up/down is never communicated by color alone, in either tier. Every up/down value carries an arrow, explicit sign, or positional cue; every statement-card sentiment carries a check/warn/neutral glyph. Color is reinforcement, never the signal.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Pure black and pure white are forbidden. Light neutrals tint warm (hue ~60-75); dark neutrals tint cool (hue ~240). Never #000, never #fff.

rules.name: The Dark-Mode Parity Rule
rules.body: Dark is the default since v4 (defaultTheme=dark, enableSystem=false). Every token has a paired dark value; the theme toggle is a 2-state dark <-> light swap (the v3 system->light->dark cycle was retired).

rules.name: The Sans-Working, Serif-Display Rule (v4)
rules.body: The working surface is IBM Plex Sans (Plex Mono for inline code + macro tickers). IBM Plex Serif is the only sanctioned second family, display-only: the portfolio masthead h1, the dividend income hero, and the ƒ ex-div glyph. Replaces the v3 One Family Rule. A serif heading outside those three roles, or any serif paragraph, is a regression. No third family.

rules.name: The Tabular-Numbers Rule
rules.body: All numeric data uses tabular figures. Body text keeps tabular off so prose reads naturally; the .tabular class is opt-in on every numeric cell, header, and data caption.

rules.name: The Same-Gravity Rule
rules.body: A 0.2% move and a 5% move share the same typographic treatment. Magnitude is read from the digits, not from size.

rules.name: The Lowercase-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Navigation tabs and chrome labels render lowercase. The label cap above each block is the only uppercase element in the system.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces have no shadow at rest. If a hover state ever introduces shadow, it is hairline and reserved for genuinely interactive elements.

rules.name: The Shadowless-Card Rule (v4)
rules.body: The v4 rounded-xl SWS cards (bg-surface-raised + 1px rule border) are real containers but never float: no box-shadow, no hover-lift, no z-translate. Depth reads from the surface->surface-raised tonal step + the hairline border. Rounded corners (rounded-xl 12px, rounded-full for chips/dots/markers) are the one visual concession; the v3 rounded-sm 2px still applies to the notes textarea + drill-in inner frames.

rules.name: The No-Floating-Cards Rule
rules.body: Cards are allowed (v4 added bordered rounded-xl SWS cards for the portfolio study tabs) but they never float: no shadow, no z-lift, no blur. The glance surfaces (/, /watchlist, the holdings register) still default to sections divided by spacing and a hairline rule, not a card grid. The drill-in stays full-bleed within the row it expands from.

rules.name: The Color-Only Transitions Rule
rules.body: Transitions animate color and opacity. Never transform, never layout properties. Numbers do not animate in or out; they update.

rules.name: The Hand-Rolled-SVG Rule
rules.body: Charts that ship in SSR HTML are hand-rolled SVG (sparkline, donut, concentration/currency stacks, benchmark line, snowflake radar, dividend stacked bar). price-chart.tsx (the drill-in 90-day chart) is the only Recharts surface; the v4 performance-chart-card embeds the hand-rolled benchmark-chart, not Recharts.

rules.name: The Same-Caption Rule
rules.body: Every block opens with the text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.06em] text-quiet caption. Recurrence is the affordance.

rules.name: The Drill-In-Not-Modal Rule
rules.body: A row's depth is reached by expanding inline, not by opening a modal or navigating to a sub-page.

dos: Do keep the accent under 10% of any screen. Its rarity is the point.
Do pair every gain/loss color with an arrow and explicit sign. Color is reinforcement, never the signal.
Do add the .tabular class to every numeric cell, header, and caption. Body text stays non-tabular.
Do tint every neutral toward the warm surface family. Chroma 0.005-0.01. No #000. No #fff.
Do treat a 5% move and a 0.2% move with the same typographic gravity.
Do scale glance-density to study-density by drilling in, not by switching to a different layout.
Do keep prose at 65-75ch line length where prose runs long.
Do reach for full borders or background tint when separation is needed.
Do ship hand-rolled SVG for any chart that lives in SSR HTML; reserve Recharts for lazy-mounted drill-ins.
Do open every block with the text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.06em] text-quiet caption. The recurrence is the affordance.
Do keep advisor copy plain-English: never buy, sell, hold, trim, add, target, forecast, predict, recommend, you should, rally, surge, soar, crash.
donts: Don't become a Bloomberg / MarketWatch full-clone. Twenty widgets, blinking tickers, every metric possible.
Don't use the crypto neon-on-black hype look. Hot pink / cyan on near-black, glow effects.
Don't become Robinhood. No gotcha-green, no candy gradients, no confetti, no big-number-flex hero.
Don't ship the generic LLM-default SaaS dashboard. No Inter, no slate-blue, no cards-nested-in-cards.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or alerts.
Don't apply background-clip: text with a gradient. Use a single solid color, with emphasis through weight.
Don't apply backdrop-filter: blur decoratively. No glassmorphism unless purposeful and rare.
Don't give the v4 rounded-xl SWS cards a box-shadow, hover-lift, or z-translate. They earn depth from the surface-raised tonal step + rule hairline only.
Don't build a hero-metric template (huge number, small label, supporting stats, gradient accent).
Don't repeat identical card grids. Same-sized cards with icon + heading + text endlessly is a layout failure.
Don't reach for a modal as the first thought. Exhaust inline and progressive (drill-in) alternatives first.
Don't animate prices in or out. Numbers updating is the data doing its job.
Don't animate transform or layout. Color and opacity only, ≤200ms.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing. Ease out with exponential curves.
Don't use em dashes in copy. Use commas, colons, semicolons, periods, or parentheses.

Don't introduce a second sans family, or use IBM Plex Serif beyond its three display roles (portfolio h1, dividend income hero, ƒ ex-div glyph). Plex Sans is the working voice, Plex Mono is for inline code + macro tickers, Plex Serif is a rare display accent. No serif paragraphs.
